summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: The package is a stub shim scoped to @ecg-internal that ships a postinstall script (node beacon.cjs) and a main entry both invoking a fire() routine. On install and on import, beacon.cjs POSTs host identifiers — hostname, install path, cwd, and node version — to the hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The destination is an IP literal with no TLS and no first-party domain. index.js exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, so builds consuming the real internal package name complete silently while the beacon fires. The stub-plus-beacon shape in an internal-looking scope is the canonical dependency-confusion reconnaissance payload: identifying internal build systems that resolve the public name, and leaking installer host metadata to a non-first-party endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
